chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ali ibn al-Rayyan, from Ahmad ibn Abi Khalaf, the mawla of Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who had bought him, his father, his mother, and his brother, so he freed them, and he contracted Ahmad (to pay for his freedom) and made him his butler.

So Ahmad said: 'The women of Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), when they would incense, would take a pit from the pits of al-Sayhani dates, cleaned of the date flesh, removing the date flesh and the peel, and cast it upon the fire before the incense. When the pit had smoked a little smoke, they would throw the pit away and then incense. They would say:

key_terms.الصَّيْحَانِيُّ: A variety of high-quality dates from Sayhan (Syria)

ai.seo_question: What was the traditional method used by the Ahl al-Bayt to enhance the fragrance of incense?
ai.summary: This hadith highlights the refined domestic customs of the Ahl al-Bayt, specifically the wives of Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him), who utilized the pits of Sayhani dates as a natural incense base to enhance the fragrance and longevity of their burning incense. This practice reflects the broader Shia emphasis on cleanliness (taharah) and the appreciation of sensory beauty in daily life, demonstrating how the Imams' households integrated practical wisdom with spiritual elegance. It serves as a precedent for using natural, pure materials to elevate the atmosphere of the home, aligning with the Prophetic tradition of loving pleasant scents.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from Ali Bin Al Rayyan, 
(It has been narrated) from Ahmad Bin Abu Khalaf, a slave of Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, and he<sup>asws</sup> had bought his father, and his mother, and his brother, so he<sup>asws</sup> had freed them, and he<sup>asws</sup> had contracted Ahmad and made him his<sup>asws</sup> butler.

So Ahmad said, ‘When the wives of Abu Al-Hassanasws incensed, they took a type from a type of Al-Saykhani date, unrefined dates, and the peels, so they would cast these upon the fire before the incense. So when the dates smoked a little smoke, they threw the dates and burnt the incense from afterwards, and it tended to hand and be more remaining, and more aromatic for the vapour, and they used to instruct with these’.
en.sarwar: 5. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from Ali ibn al-Rayyan from Ahmad ibn abu Khalaf Mawla’ of abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, whom he (the Imam) had bought along with his parents and brother then set them free but Ahmad made a contract with him (the Imam) and became his agent. He has said the following:

“Women of abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, when burning incense first took the date-stone of Sayhaniy (a certain kind of date of al-Madinah) date, clean of date fruit or sweetness and peel, then placed it on the fire before the incense. When the date-stones smoked the minimum they threw away the date-stones and burnt the incense. They said, ‘It clings with better fragrance and nicer incense’ and they instructed with this method.”
